6.1.m: A long vowel (dīrgha) replaces [the vowel] of the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) of [roots of the class] headed by tuj.
[Reduplication takes place] before liṭ of an unreduplicated verbal root (dhātu).
Vocalisation (samprasāraṇa) of [the suffix] ṣyaṅ occurs before putra and pati in a tatpuruṣa compound.
[Vocalisation occurs] of [the verbal roots] vac, svap, and those beginning with yaj, before [an affix] having the marker k (kit).
And [vocalisation occurs] of grah, jyā, ve, vyadh, vaś, vyac, vraśc, prach, and bhrajj before [an affix] having the marker ṅ (ṅit) as well [as k].
[Vocalisation occurs] of svap, syam, and vye before yaṅ.
Sphī is [the substitute] for sphāy before a past participle affix (niṣṭhā).
[Sphī is the substitute] for śyā [before niṣṭhā] when liquid state or touch [is denoted].
[The vocalisation] of [the root śyai-] preceded by abhi or ava is an optional rule (vibhāṣā).
Apaspṛdhethām, ānṛcuḥ, ānṛhuḥ, cicyuṣe, tityāja, śrātāḥ, śritam, āśīḥ, and āśīrtāḥ [are irregularly formed in sacred texts].
[Long ā is not the substitute] of the roots sphur- and sphul- before ghañ.
[Long ā is not the substitute] of the root sidh- in a meaning that is not other-worldly.
And [long ā is the substitute] of the roots mī-, mi-, and dīṅ- before lyap.

Pad-, dat-, nas-, mās-, hṛd-, niś-, asan-, yūṣan-, doṣan-, yakan-, śakan-, udan-, and āsan- [are the respective substitutes for pāda-, danta-, nāsikā-, māsa-, hṛdaya-, niśā-, asṛj-, yūṣa-, doṣa-, yakṛt-, śakṛt-, udaka-, and āsya-] before the accusative plural ending śas and subsequent endings.
A single consonant affix consisting of su-, ti-, or si- is elided after a consonant or after the long feminine affixes ṅī and āp.
The augment tuk [is inserted] after a short vowel before a primary affix (kṛt) marked with p.
Kṣayya- and jayya- [are irregularly derived] in the sense of what is possible.
Before the first two case endings (nominative and accusative), a sound homogeneous with the preceding [is the single substitute].
[A final eṅ remains] unchanged inside a verse foot (pāda), when [a short a follows which is] not preceded by v or y.
[And in a Yajus formula, eṅ remains unchanged when] preceded by āpaḥ, juṣāṇaḥ, vṛṣṇaḥ, varṣiṣṭhe, amba, ambāla, or ambikā.
In sacred poetry (chandas), the particle āṅ becomes nasalised [before a vowel].
According to Śākalya, an ik vowel before a non-homogeneous vowel [remains unchanged] and becomes short.
There is elision of su of etad and tad, provided they have no akac, before a consonant, except in a negative compound.
There is elision of saḥ even before a vowel, if it is for completing the verse foot.
After the prefixes sam, pari, and upa, [the augment suṭ is inserted before] kṛ in the meaning of adorning.
[The augment suṭ is inserted before kīr] after apa, in the case of quadrupeds and birds, in the sense of scratching.
Aparasparaḥ is formed irregularly in the sense of continuity of action.
Praskaṇva and hariścandra are formed irregularly as names of ṛṣis.
Maskara and maskarin are formed irregularly in the senses of bamboo and wandering mendicant respectively.
Kāstīra and ajastunda are formed irregularly as names of cities.
An inflected word has a low-pitched accent, with the exception of one [vowel].
Optionally (anyatarasyām), in a non-obligatory compound, [an inflectional ending has a high-pitched accent] after a final member having a high-pitched final vowel.
In sacred poetry (chandas), a non-sarvanāmasthāna inflectional ending [has a high-pitched accent] after añc.
[A non-strong inflectional ending has a high-pitched accent] after ūṭh, idam, the stems substituted for pad etc., ap, pum, rai, and dyu.
[An inflectional ending] beginning with a consonant [has a high-pitched accent] after the ṣaṣ-class, tri, and catur.
[An inflectional ending beginning with a consonant does] not [have a high-pitched accent] after go, śvan, sāvavarṇa, rāṭ, aṅ, kruṅ, or primary derivatives (kṛt).
A sārvadhātuka affix replacing l-affixes is low-pitched after [a base ending in] tāsi, or after what has an instruction of anudātta-it, ṅ-it, or ad-upadeśa, except in the case of hnu and iṅ.
[A sārvadhātuka affix is low-pitched] before a vowel without the augment iṭ after svap etc. and hiṃs.
[The vowel] preceding the affix in bhī, hrī, bhṛ, hu, mad, jan, dhan, daridrā, and jāgṛ [has a high-pitched accent] before an affix with the marker p.
The initial [vowel has a high-pitched accent] optionally (anyatarasyām) before [the affix] ṇamul.
[The initial syllable] of pathin and mathin [has a high-pitched accent] before a strong case ending (sarvanāmasthāna).
[The initial syllable has a high-pitched accent before] the affix ṇyat after īḍ, vand, vṛ, śaṃs, and duh.
[The initial syllable has a high-pitched accent] optionally (vibhāṣā) in the words veṇu and indhāna.
[The initial syllable has a high-pitched accent in the words] tyāga, rāga, hāsa, kuha, śvaṭha, and kratha.

6.2.m: In a bahuvrīhi compound, the prior member retains its original accent.

In a tatpuruṣa compound, [the prior member retains its original accent before members meaning] equal, [or when governed by endings of] the instrumental, the locative, an object of comparison, an indeclinable, the accusative, or a gerundive (kṛtya).
[The word] pratibandhin [retains its original accent] in the sense of a long time or distress.
[The prior member retains its original accent] before adhvaryu and kaṣāya, when denoting a genus.
[The prior member retains its original accent] before sa-dṛśa and pratirūpa, in the sense of likeness.
[The prior member retains its original accent] before mātrā, upajñā, upakrama, and chāyā, when neuter.
[The prior member retains its original accent] before savidha, sanīḍa, samaryāda, saveśa, and sadeśa, in the sense of vicinity.
[The prior member retains its original accent] before words ending in the affixes śra, jya, avama, kan, and pāpa, or ending in vat, in an abstract noun in a karmadhāraya compound.
In a dvigu compound, [the prior member retains its original accent] before words ending in ik, kāla, kapāla, bhagāla, and śarāva.
A word ending in a locative case (saptamī) [retains its original accent] before siddha, śuṣka, pakva, and bandha, except after a word denoting time.
In a dvandva compound of kṣatriya names in the plural, [the prior member retains its original accent] among Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis.
Mahān [retains its original accent] before vrīhi, aparāhṇa, gṛṣṭi, iṣvāsa, jābāla, bhāra, bhārata, hailihila, raurava, and pravṛddha.
And kṣullaka [retains its original accent as prior member] in the vaiśvadeva sacrifice.
Go [retains its original accent as prior member] before sāda, sādi, and sārathi.
Kurugārhapata, riktaguru, asūtajaratī, aślīladṛḍharūpā, pārevaḍavā, taitilakadrū, paṇyakambala, and the dāsībhāra class [retain the original accent of the prior member].
A gati not ending in ik [retains its original accent] before the root añc- followed by the affix va.
A measure of gold [retains its original accent as prior member] when denoting wealth.
Katara and katama [retain their original accent as prior member] in a karmadhāraya compound.
Ārya [retains its original accent as prior member] before brāhmaṇa and kumāra.
Saptamī and hārin [have the initial high-pitched accent] when lawful, meaning non-taking.
The words dīrgha, kāśa, tuṣa, bhrāṣṭra, and vaṭa [retain their original accent] before a word ending in the affix ja.
In a word of many syllables, the vowel preceding the final [vowel is high-pitched].
[A first member which is] not having vṛddhi grade on its first syllable and not belonging to the class headed by karkī [has the accent on the penultimate vowel] before prastha.
[A first member which is] not mahat and not nava [has the penultimate high-pitched] before nagara, among non-northerners.
Not so for the words hāstina, phalaka, and mārdeya [before pura].
The words kusūla, kūpa, kumbha, and śālā [have the final vowel high-pitched] before bila [‘hole’].
And the word sarva [has its final vowel high-pitched] when the subsequent member has undergone vṛddhi grade.
After the negative particle nañ, [the initial vowel of] jara, mara, mitra, and mṛta [is high-pitched].
In the sacred texts (chandas), a disyllabic word [after su] has its initial vowel high-pitched.
In a dvigu compound, [the initial vowel of] kiṃsa, mantha, śūrpa, pāyya, and kāṇḍa [is high-pitched].
In a tatpuruṣa compound of the neuter gender, [the initial vowel of] śālā [is high-pitched].
[The initial vowel of] cela, kheṭa, kaṭuka, and kāṇḍa [is high-pitched] when expressing censure.
[The final syllable of the second member retains its natural accent before] palala, sūpa, and śāka, when denoting a mixture.
Not after designations of teachers, kings, priests, associated persons, or kinsmen.
Both [members retain their original accents] simultaneously in vanaspati and the rest.
Not when the second member begins with a low-pitched accent, except before pṛthivī, rudra, pūṣan, and manthin.
And [the first member has its final syllable accented before datta and śruta] when expressing ‘done by one who has become such’.
[The first member has its final syllable accented before a word ending in affix] an denoting state or action.
Optionally (vibhāṣā) before words ending in tṛn, anna, tīkṣṇa, and śuci [the negative particle nañ has its final syllable accented].
In a bahuvrīhi compound, [the words] idam, etad, and tad, when counting repetitions of an action, [have their final syllable accented] before ordinal numerals and prathama.
Not after an indeclinable, a directional word, go, mahat, sthūla, muṣṭi, pṛthu, or vatsa.
A word ending in the past participle affix, except kṛta, mita, and pratipanna, [has its final syllable accented] after a genus term, a time word, sukha and the rest, when not denoting clothing.
When ending in a short vowel, the [syllable] preceding the final [has the high-pitched accent].
After bahu, like the negative particle nañ, when the second member denotes a plurality.
After a preverb, an inalienable body part that is motionless, except a rib, [has its final syllable accented].
[The word] maṇḍala, when denoting that which exists all around, [has its final syllable accented] after pari.
[After] anu, a non-principal younger [female relative takes high-pitched accent on the initial syllable].
In a tatpuruṣa compound after prati, words beginning with aṃśū [take high-pitched accent on the initial syllable].
After upa, a disyllabic word and ajina, excluding words beginning with gaura, [take high-pitched accent on the initial syllable].
After dvi and tri, before pād, dant, and mūrdhan in a bahuvrīhi compound [high-pitched accent falls on the initial syllable].
In the Sacred Texts, the initial syllable of the subsequent word diversely [takes high-pitched accent].

6.3.m: [There is non-elision] of the ablative ending after words beginning with stoka.
[There is non-elision] of the instrumental ending after ojas, sahas, ambhas, and tamas.
[There is non-elision] of the dative ending in designations used by grammarians.
And according to the Easterners, before a consonant-initial member when denoting the name of a prison.
[There is non-elision of the locative ending] after a word denoting one's own body-part other than mūrdhan and mastaka, when not followed by kāma.
In a tatpuruṣa compound before a primary affix, diversely [there is non-elision of the locative ending].
[There is non-elision of the locative ending] of prāvṛṣ, śapad, kāla, and divā before ja.
[There is non-elision of the locative ending] before śaya, vāsa, and vāsin, except after kāla.
[There is non-elision of the genitive ending] after stems ending in ṛ that denote relations based on sacred knowledge or birth.
Īt is [the substitute for the final vowel] of agni before soma and varuṇa [in a dvandva compound of deities].
And in the Veda (chandas), pitarā-mātarā [is validly formed].

A feminine stem which has a masculine counterpart of the same form and meaning and does not end in ūṅ is treated like a masculine (puṃvat) before a coreferential member (samānādhikaraṇa) in the feminine, provided it does not end in an ordinal suffix (pūraṇī) or belong to the class beginning with priyā.
[A feminine stem is treated like a masculine] before [taddhita affixes] beginning with tasil up to kṛtvasuc.
And [a feminine stem] formed with a taddhita affix that causes vṛddhi grade [is not treated like a masculine], except when denoting a dyed thing or a modification.
[A stem] is treated like a masculine in a karmadhāraya compound and before [the secondary affixes] jātīyar and deśīya.
A stem of more than one syllable ending in a ṅī affix is shortened (hrasva) before the affixes gha, rūpa, kalpa, celaṭ, bruva, gotra, mata, and hata.
Āt is [the substitute for the final vowel] of mahat before a coreferential member (samānādhikaraṇa) and before [the affix] jātīyar.
[The substitution is] optionally (vibhāṣā) for all [these] before numerals beginning with catvāriṃśat ('forty').
Hṛt is [the substitute] of hṛdaya before lekha, the affix yat, the affix aṇ, and lāsa.
And [uda is optionally the substitute of udaka] before mantha, odana, saktu, bindu, vajra, bhāra, hāra, vīvadha, and gāha.
According to Gālava, a vowel of the ik pratyāhāra not ending in ṅī is shortened (hrasva) [in a compound].
Mum is [the augment] of arus, dviṣat, and that which ends in a vowel (ac) [before an affix with kh as marker].
[An augment mum is added] to a monosyllabic word ending in the ic pratyāhāra, and it is treated as having the accusative affix am.
[Nañ remains] in its original form (prakṛtyā) in nabhrāj, napāt, navedā, nāsatyā, namuci, nakula, nakha, napuṃsaka, nakṣatra, nakra, and nāka.
Naga is optionally (anyatarasyām) [formed] when not referring to living beings (aprāṇin).
[The substitute sa occurs for samāna] when jyotis, janapada, rātri, nābhi, nāman, gotra, rūpa, sthāna, varṇa, varya, vacana, or bandhu follows.

6.3.s: viṣvag-devayoś ca ṭer adry añcatau vapratyaye ||
6.3.d: विष्वग्-देवयोश् च टेर् अद्र्य् अञ्चतौ वप्रत्यये ॥
6.3.m: And the substitute adri occurs for the final segment beginning with the last vowel (ṭi) of viṣvak and deva, before añcu followed by an affix with elided v.
[The substitute] sadha occurs [for saha] in sacred texts when māda or stha follows.
Long ī occurs for the [a of] ap after dvi, antar, and prefixes.
The letter o [replaces] the non-high vowel a of [the verbal roots] sah and vah [upon elision of ḍh].
[A long vowel replaces the final vowel of] a mark on an ear [consisting in words other than] aviṣṭa, aṣṭa, pañca, maṇi, bhinna, chinna, chidra, sruva, and svastika [before the secondary affix ya].
[A long vowel replaces the vowel of the verbal roots] nah, vṛt, vṛṣ, vyadh, ruc, sah, and tan before [the affix] kvi.
Before [the secondary affix] matup, [a long vowel replaces the final vowel of a stem] having many vowels, except ajira, etc.
[The final vowel] of a prefix is variously lengthened before [a root with the affix] ghañ, when not referring to a human being.
And [the final vowel] of [the word] oṣadhi [is lengthened in a sacred formula] before an inflectional ending other than the nominative.
In a verse (ṛc), [the vowel] of tu, nu, gha, makṣu, taṅku, tra, and uruṣyā [is lengthened].

6.4.m: [A long vowel replaces the penultimate a] of a consonant cluster ending in s and of the stem mahat [before a non-vocative sarvanāmasthāna].
[A long vowel replaces the penultimate vowel before a non-vocative sarvanāmasthāna] of the words ap, [those ending in] tṛn or tṛc, and svasṛ, naptṛ, neṣṭṛ, tvaṣṭṛ, kṣattṛ, hotṛ, potṛ, and praśāstṛ.
[A long vowel replaces the penultimate vowel] of an element ending in a nasal before kvip or an affix beginning with a jhal consonant, when marked with k or ṅ.
And [ūṭh replaces] the penultimate vowel of jvar, tvar, sriv, av, and mav [before an affix beginning with a nasal or jhal, marked with k or ṅ].
[Elision takes place] of the penultimate nasal of consonants belonging to roots not marked with an i marker, before [an affix] marked with k or ṅ.
[Elision of the penultimate nasal takes place] of daṃś, sañj, and svañj before [the class affix] śap.
And [elision of the penultimate nasal of rañj takes place] before [the affix] ghañ expressing action or instrument.

Elision of the nasal occurs for roots whose original grammatical instruction has an anudātta vowel, for van, and for roots beginning with tan, before an affix beginning with a non-nasal stop or sibilant (jhal) having a k-marker or an ṅ-marker.
[The substitute ā occurs for the nasal] of jan, san, and khan before san and affixes beginning with a non-nasal stop or sibilant (jhal).

6.4.s: sanaḥ ktici lopaś ca asya anyatarasyām ||
6.4.d: सनः क्तिचि लोपश् च अस्य अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

6.4.m: Lengthening occurs for yu and plu in sacred texts [before an ārdhadhātuka affix].

6.4.s: sya-sic-sīyuṭ-tāsiṣu bhāva-karmaṇor upadeśe 'j-jhana-graha-dṛśāṃ vā ciṇvad-iṭ ca ||
6.4.d: स्य-सिच्-सीयुट्-तासिषु भाव-कर्मणोर् उपदेशे ऽज्-झन-ग्रह-दृशां वा चिण्वद्-इट् च ॥
6.4.m: Optionally (vā), in the reflexive-passive and passive (bhāva and karman), before sya, sic, sīyuṭ, and tāsi, the augment iṭ like ciṇ occurs for roots taught in original grammatical instruction as ending in a vowel, for han, grah, and dṛś.
Short i is optionally (anyatarasyām) substituted [for the ā] of mayati (meṅ) [before lyap].
The augment aṭ, with high-pitched accent, is prefixed [to a verbal root] before luṅ, laṅ, and lṛṅ.
Variously in the sacred texts, even when not in connection with māṅ.
Before a vowel, iyaṅ and uvaṅ are substituted respectively for the i and u of the affix śnu, of a verbal root, and of bhrū-.
[yaṇ is substituted for u] of hu- and śnu before a sārvadhātuka affix [beginning with a vowel].
Before ciṇ and ṇamul, a long vowel (dīrgha) [substitutes for the penultimate of roots with marker m] optionally (anyatarasyām).
[A short vowel substitutes for the penultimate] of chad- before [the affix] gha, when not preceded by two prefixes (upasarga).
Elision (lopa) [of the penultimate vowel a] occurs in gam-, han-, jan-, khan-, and ghas- before an affix marked with k or ṅ, when [the augment] aṅ is not present.
In the Veda (chandasi), [hi becomes dhi] after śru-, śṛṇu-, pṝ-, kṛ-, and vṛ-.
And [zero-replacement (luk) of hi occurs] after the affix u not preceded by a consonant cluster (saṃyoga).
e replaces [the vowel of] ghu roots and as- before [the ending hi replaced by] dhi, and elision (lopa) of the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) occurs.

In the perfect (liṭ), e replaces [short] a occurring between single consonants in a stem whose initial is not a substitute (adeśa), [and elision of the reduplicative syllable occurs before a k- or ṅ-marked affix].
And [e replaces a and the reduplicative syllable is elided before thal with iṭ or a k- or ṅ-marked liṭ affix] in tṝ-, phal-, bhaj-, and trap-.
Not [so] in śas-, dad-, or stems beginning with v, or stems having a guṇa grade (guṇa).
[Vocalisation occurs] of śvan-, yuvan-, and maghavan-, when not followed by a secondary affix (taddhita).
[Elision of a of an occurs] of han- preceded by a word ending in a case affix (ṣapūrva) and of dhṛtarājan- before the secondary affix aṇ.
In Vedic mantras, [elision occurs of the initial ā] of ātmán- beginning with the instrumental case affix āṅ.
And [there is elision of the y] denoting a patronymic before a taddhita affix, but not before [one beginning with] a vowel.
Of sthūla, dūra, yuvan, hrasva, kṣipra, and kṣudra, the portion beginning with the semivowel is dropped, and the preceding [vowel takes] guṇa grade.

In place of priya, sthira, sphira, uru, bahula, guru, vṛddha, tṛpra, dīrgha, and vṛndāraka, [the substitutes] pra, stha, spha, var, baṃhi, gar, varṣi, trab, drāghi, and vṛnda [are substituted respectively].
And [the bases] gāthin, vidathin, keśin, gaṇin, and paṇin [remain in their original form before aṇ signifying a descendant].
Not so when preceded by m, before [an affix] denoting a descendant, with the exception of carman.
The words ṛtvya, vāstvya, vāstva, mādhvī, and hiraṇyaya [are irregularly formed] in sacred texts.

7.1.m: aś is substituted for ṅas after yuṣmad and asmad.
tātaṅ is optionally (anyatarasyām) substituted for tu and hi in benediction.
In a compound whose prior member is not a negative particle (nañ), lyap is substituted for ktvā.
And tap, tan, aptan, athan, and thana [are substituted in the sacred texts for thas and tha].
[The augment asuk is added] to aśva-, kṣīra-, vṛṣa-, and lavaṇa- in the sense of self-gratification before kyac.
In the sacred texts, [nuṭ is added to ām] after śrī- and grāmaṇī-.
[The augment num is] not [added to labh-] after su- and dur- by themselves [before khal and ghañ].
[The augment num is inserted] before a sarvanāmasthāna affix for [stems] having the marker u, ṛ, or ḷ, and for añc, provided they are not a verbal root.
[The augment num is inserted] for a neuter [stem base ending in] a consonant of the jhal pratyāhāra or a vowel [before a sarvanāmasthāna affix].
According to Gālava, [a neuter stem base] whose masculine counterpart is spoken behaves like a masculine before [inflectional endings] beginning with the instrumental [singular].
For asthi, dadhi, sakthi, and akṣi, the high-pitched substitute anaṅ [replaces the final vowel before inflectional endings beginning with the instrumental and following vowels].
[The augment num is inserted] in the Veda for dṛś, svavas, and svatavas [before su].
āt is substituted [for the final vowel] of pathin, mathin, and ṛbhukṣin [before a sarvanāmasthāna affix].
And anaṅ [is substituted before su] for stems ending in ṛ, and for uśanas, purudaṃsas, and anehas.
[kroṣṭu behaves like a stem ending in tṛc] optionally (vibhāṣā) before [inflectional endings] beginning with the instrumental [and beginning] with a vowel.
The high-pitched augment ām is inserted for catur and anaḍuh [before a sarvanāmasthāna affix].

7.2.m: vṛddhi grade occurs [for the stem vowel] before [the aorist marker] sic in the active voice endings (parasmaipada).
[vṛddhi grade before sic does not occur] for verbal roots ending in h, m, or y, nor for kṣaṇ, śvas, jāgṛ, those ending in the causative affix ṇi, śvi, and those having the marker e.
And [the augment iṭ is not inserted] before [kṛt affixes beginning with] ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka, and sa.

[The augment iṭ is not inserted before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant] following [a verbal root] that has a single vowel and is low-pitched (anudātta) in original grammatical instruction (upadeśa).
[The augment iṭ is not inserted] following kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ, stu, dru, sru, and śru before [the perfect affix of] liṭ.

kṣubdha, svānta, dhvānta, lagna, mliṣṭa, viribdha, phāṇṭa, and bāḍha are ready-formed words in the meanings churning-implement, mind, darkness, attached, unclear, sound, made without effort, and exceedingly, respectively.
[The niṣṭhā form] of kaṣ [is irregular] in the senses of difficult and impenetrable.
[The forms] dānta, śānta, pūrṇa, dasta, spaṣṭa, channa, and jñapta are optionally (vā) [irregularly formed].
[The augment iṭ is added] after snu and kram when not causing a middle voice ending (ātmanepada).
And [it is not long] before sic in the active voice endings (parasmaipada).
[The augment iṭ is optionally added] before liṅ and sic in the middle voice endings (ātmanepada).
[The augment iṭ is] optionally (vā) [added before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning with val] after svarati, sūti, sūyati, dhūñ, and [roots] having an indicatory marker (it) ū.
[The augment iṭ is optionally added] before s beginning an affix other than the aorist marker sic after kṛt (to cut), cṛt (to tie), chṛd (to vomit), tṛd (to pierce), and nṛt (to dance).
The augment iṭ [is optionally added] after gam (to go) before [an affix beginning with s] in active voice endings.
[The augment iṭ is] not [added] after the four [verbal roots] beginning with vṛdh (to grow).
[The augment iṭ is] always not [added] before thal after a verbal root ending in a vowel which is devoid of iṭ (aniṭ) in the manner of [its behaviour before] tāsi.
The augment iṭ [is added before thal] after ad (to eat), ṛ (to go), and vyay (to spend).
[The augment iṭ before vasu is] an optional rule (vibhāṣā) after gam (to go), han (to strike), vid (to know), and viś (to enter).
[The augment iṭ is added before sic] after stu (to praise), su (to press), and dhūñ (to shake) in active voice endings.
[The augment iṭ is added] before a sārvadhātuka affix beginning with a consonant [other than y] after [the verbal roots] beginning with rud (to weep).
There is elision of non-final s of liṅ.
[Long ā is the substitute of the final sound] of yuṣmad and asmad when no complete substitute is prescribed.
And [long ā is the substitute of the final of yuṣmad and asmad] before the dual of the nominative (prathamā) inflectional ending in the spoken language.
tisṛ and catasṛ are the substitutes of tri and catur in the feminine.
jaras is optionally (anyatarasyām) the substitute of jarā [before an inflectional ending beginning with a vowel].
s is the substitute of the non-final t and d of tyad and tad before su.

7.3.m: Long ā (āt) replaces [the first vowel] of devikā, śiṃśapā, dityavāh, dīrghasattra, and śreyas.

7.3.s: na y-vābhyāṃ padāntābhyāṃ pūrvau tu tābhyām aic ||
7.3.d: न य्-वाभ्यां पदान्ताभ्यां पूर्वौ तु ताभ्याम् ऐच् ॥
7.3.m: [Vṛddhi does] not [apply] to [the first vowel] preceded by y or v when at the end of a pada (padānta); but before them, ai and au (aic) [are inserted].
And [aic is inserted before the v] of nyagrodha when uncompounded (kevala).
[Vṛddhi applies to the uttarapada] designating eastern (prāñc) villages or towns.
And [vṛddhi applies to the uttarapada], as well as to the initial member (pūrvapada), when ending in hṛd, bhaga, or sindhu.
[The vowel] of the subsequent member ending in jaṅgala, dhenu, or valaja is optional (vibhāṣita) [for vṛddhi].
After ardha, [vṛddhi] of the prior member denoting a measure (parimāṇa) is optionally (vā) [applied].
Of śuci, īśvara, kṣetrajña, kuśala, and nipuṇa preceded by the negative particle nañ;
Of yathātatha and yathāpura alternately;
The augment yuk occurs [before ṇi] after śā, chā, sā, hvā, vyā, ve, and pā;

7.3.s: pratyayasthāt kāt pūrvasya ata id āpy asupaḥ ||
7.3.d: प्रत्ययस्थात् कात् पूर्वस्य अत इद् आप्य् असुपः ॥

7.3.m: According to the Northern teachers, [short i is substituted] in place of long ā preceded by ya or ka;
Bhuja and nyubja are irregularly formed to signify 'hand' and 'disease' respectively.
And [a velar does not substitute before ṇyat] for yaj-, yāc-, ruc-, pravac-, and ṛc-.
Prayojya and niyojya [are irregularly formed with a palatal] in the sense of 'capable'.
Zero-replacement (luk) [of the affix ksa] optionally (vā) occurs for duh-, dih-, lih-, and guh- before a dental middle voice ending.
For the eight [roots] beginning with śam-, a long vowel [replaces the vowel] before śyan.
For kram-, [a long vowel replaces the vowel before an affix marked with ś] before active voice endings.
Piba, jighra, dhama, tiṣṭha, mana, yaccha, paśya, ṛccha, dhau, śīya, and sīda replace pā-, ghrā-, dhmā-, sthā-, mnā-, dāṇ-, dṛś-, ṛ-, sṛ-, śad-, and sad- respectively [before an affix marked with ś].
And [guṇa grade replaces the penultimate short vowel] of a base ending in the augment puk or having a light penultimate vowel [before a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka affix].
[The augment īṭ is added] to tu-, ru-, stu-, śam-, and am- before a sārvadhātuka affix [beginning with a consonant].
A short vowel replaces [the final vowel] of words meaning 'mother' and of stem bases termed nadī [before the vocative singular affix].
[Guṇa grade replaces final] ṛ before ṅi and a sarvanāmasthāna affix.
Optionally (vibhāṣā) after dvitīya and tṛtīya;

7.4.m: The penultimate vowel is shortened before ṇi followed by caṅ;
Optionally (anyatarasyām) in the case of bhrāj, bhās, bhāṣ, dīp, jīv, mīl, and pīḍ;
And guṇa grade replaces an initial cluster ending in ṛ;
Guṇa grade replaces [the vowel of] śīṅ before a sārvadhātuka affix;
A short vowel replaces [the vowel of] ūh after a prefix (upasarga);
Lengthening takes place before a non-kṛt sārvadhātuka affix;
Not in the Veda in the case of aputra- [before kyac].
durasyuḥ, draviṇasyuḥ, vṛṣaṇyati, and riṣaṇyati [are irregularly formed in the Veda].
[Long vowel ā is substituted for the final vowel] of deva- and sumna- in the sacrificial formula of the Kāṭhaka school.
[Short vowel] i [is the substitute] of do- ('to cut'), so- ('to bind'), mā- ('to measure'), and sthā- ('to stand'), before an affix beginning with t and having marker k.
And sudhita-, vasudhita-, nemadhita-, dhiṣva, and dhiṣīya [are irregularly formed in the Veda].
Before [the affix] san, is is [the substitute] of the vowel of mī-, mā-, [roots of the class] ghu, rabh-, labh-, śak-, pat-, and pad-.
There is optionally (vā) guṇa grade [of the vowel] of an intransitive muc- [before san].

And dādharti, dardharti, dardharṣi, bobhūtu, tetikte, alarṣi, āpanīphaṇat, saṃsaniṣyadat, karikrat, kanikradat, bharibhrat, davidhvataḥ, davidyutat, taritrataḥ, sarīsṛpatam, varīvṛjat, marmṛjya, and āganīganti [are irregularly formed in the Veda].

[Short vowel i is] optionally (vā) [the substitute of the vowel of the reduplicative syllable] of sru- ('to flow'), śru- ('to hear'), dru- ('to run'), pru- ('to spring'), plu- ('to float'), and cyu- ('to move') [before san].
nīk is [the augment of the reduplicative syllable] of vañc-, sraṃs-, dhvaṃs-, bhraṃs-, kas-, pat-, pad-, and skand- [before yaṅ and yaṅ-luk].
nuk is [the augment of the reduplicative syllable ending] in a short vowel a of [a root] ending in a nasal [before yaṅ and yaṅ-luk].
And [nuk is the augment of the reduplicative syllable ending in a short vowel a] of jap-, jabh-, dah-, daś-, bhañj-, and paś- [before yaṅ and yaṅ-luk].
When can follows which is followed by a light [vowel], [the reduplicative syllable behaves] like that before san, provided there has been no elision of an aṅ [sound-segment].
Short a [replaces the penultimate or vowel of the stems] smṛ, dṝ, tvara, pratha, mrada, stṝ, and spaś.

8.1.m: [There is doubling] of upari, adhi, and adhas in the sense of proximity (sāmīpya).
[The doubled expression behaves] like a karmadhāraya compound in the following cases.
[There is doubling] of an adjective (guṇavacana) in the sense of similarity in quality (prakāra).
[There is doubling] optionally (anyatarasyām) of priya and sukha in the sense of easiness (akṛcchra).
The dvandva compound is doubled in the senses of secret, defining a boundary, transgression, use of sacrificial vessels, and manifest expression.
The entire [word becomes] low-pitched accent (anudātta), except at the beginning of a metrical quarter (pāda).
vām and nau [are substituted] for yuṣmad and asmad in the genitive, dative, and accusative [dual].
vas and nas [are substituted] for the plural.
[The substitute applies] optionally (vibhāṣā) to [an inflected word occurring after] a nominative (prathamā) preceded by another word.
[A finite verb is not anudātta] when connected with the particles yat, yadi, hanta, kuvit, net, cet, caṇ, kaccit, and yatra.
In the Veda (chandas), even multiple [finite verbs] dependent [on hi retain their accent].
[Nor] kiṃ in asking about an action, provided it is without a prefix and not negated.
And an interrogative pronoun (kiṃvṛtta) followed by cit.

8.1.s: gatyartha-loṭā lṛṇ na cet kārakaṃ sarvānyat ||
8.1.d: गत्यर्थ-लोटा लृण् न चेत् कारकं सर्वान्यत् ॥
8.1.m: A simple future (lṛṭ) [connected] with an imperative (loṭ) of a verb of motion is not [anudātta], unless the case-role (kāraka) is entirely different.
[An imperative verb] accompanied by a prefix, non-first person, is optionally [accentless] (vibhāṣā).
After āma, a vocative separated by one [word is accentless], when not near.
In the Veda, [the vocative is accentless] when followed by yat, hi, or tu.
After eka and anya, syntactically related.
After a word expressing praise, a praised word is low-pitched accent, [and likewise words] after kāṣṭha and the rest.
And [a word ending] in a case-affix [is low-pitched accent] in censure, if not beginning with a gotra-suffix.
A preceding vocative is treated as non-existent.
Before a co-referential vocative, a general term is not [treated as non-existent].
A plural word before a specific term is optionally [treated as non-existent] (vibhāṣā).

8.2.m: For a low-pitched accent following a semi-vowel substituted for a high-pitched or circumflex accent, there is circumflex accent.
Or optionally (vā) circumflex accent when a low-pitched accent at the beginning of an inflected word follows.
There is elision of n at the end of a nominal stem.
āsandīvat, aṣṭhīvat, cakrīvat, kakṣīvat, rumaṇvat, and carmaṇvatī [are irregularly formed with v].
Optionally (vā) of druh, muh, snuh, and snih.
ṣ is substituted for [the finals of] vraśc, bhrasj, sṛj, mṛj, yaj, rāj, bhrāj, and stems ending in ch or ś.
In a monosyllabic stem ending in a voiced aspirate (jhaṣ), an unaspirated voiced stop (baś) becomes an aspirated voiced stop (bhaṣ), before s and dhv.

8.2.s: ra-dābhyāṃ niṣthāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ ||
8.2.d: र-दाभ्यां निष्थातो नः पूर्वस्य च दः ॥

8.2.m: Also [the t of a past participle affix is replaced by n] after a verbal root having a consonant cluster at its beginning, ending in ā, and containing a semivowel (yaṇ).
Vitta- [is the irregular form with t retained] in the senses of wealth and belief.
Amnar, ūdhar, and avar are used both ways in sacred literature (chandas).
And [final s] of bhuvas, being one of the great mystical utterances (mahāvyāhṛti), [is replaced by r].
Of the affix vasu, and of sraṃs-, dhvaṃs-, and anaḍuh-, [the final sound is replaced by] d [at the end of an inflected word].
A preceding vowel (ik) in the penultimate position of [a base ending in] r or v is lengthened.

8.2.d: अदसो ऽसेर् दाद् उ दो मः ॥

8.2.m: The final vowel with its following consonant (ṭi) of a sentence (vākya) becomes a protracted vowel (pluta) and is high-pitched (udātta).
When using hai or he, [protraction applies] to hai and he.

8.2.d: गुरोर् अनृतो ऽनन्त्यस्य अप्य् एकैकस्य प्राचाम् ॥

8.2.m: [Protraction applies] to the initial sound of brūhi, preṣya, śrauṣaṭ, vauṣaṭ, and āvaha.
And in an instruction directed to the Agnīdh priest, [protraction applies] also to the subsequent [syllable].
Optionally (vibhāṣā) [protraction applies] to hi in an answer to a question.
[The protracted vowel is] circumflex accent in an iterated word when expressing indignation, agreement, anger, or reproach.

8.2.s: eco 'pragṛhyasya adūrādhdūte pūrvasya ardhasya ad uttarasya+idutau ||
8.2.d: एचो ऽप्रगृह्यस्य अदूराध्दूते पूर्वस्य अर्धस्य अद् उत्तरस्य+इदुतौ ॥

8.2.m: Before a vowel in continuous phonological text, 'y' and 'v' [are substituted] for those two [short 'i' and 'u' respectively].

8.3.m: In the Veda, 'ru' [replaces the final consonant] of [the suffixes] 'matup' and 'vasu' in the vocative singular.
Here, optionally (vā), the preceding [vowel becomes] nasalised [before 'ru'].
An anusvāra occurs subsequent to [that which is not] nasalised.
[The 'n' of an inflected word replaces with 'ru'] after a long vowel when followed by 'aṭ' within the same metrical quarter.
Visarjanīya [is substituted for 'r'] before an unvoiced consonant ('khar') and at the pause.
'y' [replaces 'ru'] preceded by 'bho', 'bhago', 'agho', or 'a'/'ā', before a voiced sound ('aś').
According to Śākaṭāyana, a lighter effort of pronunciation applies to 'v' and 'y'.
The augment 'ṅamuṭ' is invariably added to a final nasal stop ('ṅam') preceded by a short vowel, before a vowel ('ac').
[Visarjanīya] in 'dvis', 'tris', and 'catur' in the sense of frequency [becomes 'ṣ'].
[Visarjanīya] not standing in a subsequent member of a compound is invariably [replaced by 'ṣ'] in a compound.
[Visarjanīya] following short 'a', not belonging to an indeclinable, [becomes 's'] before 'kṛ', 'kami', 'kaṃsa', 'kumbha', 'pātra', 'kuśā', and 'karṇī'.
[In the Veda, visarga optionally becomes a sibilant] before kaḥ, karat, karati, kṛdhi, and kṛta, except when following Aditi.
[Visarga] of an ablative ending [optionally becomes a sibilant] when para expresses the sense of an endpoint (avadhī).
[Visarga] of a genitive ending [optionally becomes a sibilant in the Veda] before pati, putra, pṛṣṭha, pāra, pada, payas, and poṣa.
[Now follows the governing rule:] A retroflex sound replaces that which does not end a pada.
Only of stu- and of roots ending in ṇi [does the s become retroflex] after the reduplicative syllable (abhyāsa) before the desiderative affix san.
And the s of svid-, svad-, and sah- [becomes retroflex after the reduplicative syllable before the desiderative affix san].
In rules prior to [the mention of] sita, even when there is an intervention by the augment aṭ.
After a preverb (upasarga), [the s] of su-, sū-, so-, stu-, stubh-, sthā-, senaya-, sidh-, sic-, sañj-, and svañj [becomes retroflex].
After pari, ni, and vi, [the s] of sev-, sita, saya, siv-, sah-, suṭ, stu-, and svañj [becomes retroflex].
After anu, vi, pari, abhi, and ni, [the s] of syand- [becomes retroflex] when referring to non-living beings.
After vi, [the s] of skand- [becomes retroflex], except before a niṣṭhā affix.
The form pariskandaḥ occurs in the sense of the Eastern Bharatas.
After nir, ni, and vi, [the s] of sphur- and sphul- [becomes retroflex].

After a stem base (aṅga) ending in [a sound of the pratyāhāra] iṇ, the dh of [the middle voice ending] ṣīdhvam, and of [the endings of] the aorist (luṅ) and perfect (liṭ), [is replaced by retroflex ḍh].
[The s of svasṛ becomes retroflex] optionally (anyatarasyām) after mātuḥ and pituḥ.
[The s] of as- followed by y or a vowel [becomes retroflex] after a preverb or prādur.
[The s] of supi, sūti, and samā [becomes retroflex] after su, vi, nir, and dur.
[The s] of snā- [becomes retroflex] after ni and nadī in the sense of skill.
[The s] of sthira [becomes retroflex] after gavi and yudhi.
[The s] of sthala [becomes retroflex] after vi, ku, śamī, and pari.
[The s] of stha [becomes retroflex] after amba, āmba, go, bhūmi, savya, apa, dvi, tri, ku, śeku, śaṅku, aṅgu, mañji, puñji, parame, barhis, divi, and agni.
[The s of stha becomes retroflex] after a short vowel before a secondary affix (taddhita) beginning with t.
[The s of nis becomes retroflex] before yuṣmat, tat, and forms of takṣ-, within a metrical line (antaḥpādam).
[The s] of stuta and stoma [becomes retroflex] in the Veda (chandasi).
And [the s] of sah- [becomes retroflex] after pṛtanā and ṛta.
[Retroflexion does] not [apply to the s] of roots containing r as following sound (rapara), of sṛp-, sṛj-, spṛś-, spṛh-, nor of savana and following words.
And [retroflexion of s occurs in the forms] pratistabdha and nistabdha.
[There is retroflexion of s] of the verbal roots stambh, siv, and sah before the aorist affix caṅ.
[There is retroflexion of s] following [the reduplication] of sad and svañj in the perfect tense (liṭ).
In the Veda, optionally (vā), [retroflexion of s occurs] after ni, vi, and abhi, even when intervened by the augment aṭ.

8.4.m: After r and ṣ, n is replaced by ṇa within the same inflected word (pada).
Even when there is intervention by the vowels and semivowels (aṭ), the velar stops (ku), the labial stops (pu), the augment āṅ, or the augment num.
[The n] of vana [is replaced by ṇa] after puragā, miśrakā, sidhrakā, śārikā, koṭara, and agra.
There is an optional rule (vibhāṣā) [for the replacement of n of vana by ṇa] after herbs and trees.
And [replacement of n by ṇa takes place] in the final sound of a nominal stem (prātipadika), in the augment num, and in inflectional endings (vibhakti).
And [the n] of ni [is replaced by ṇa after a prefix] before the verbal roots gad, nad, pat, pad, the ghu roots, mā, so, han, yā, vā, drā, psā, vap, vah, śam, ci, and dih.
In the remaining instances, there is an optional rule (vibhāṣā) in original grammatical instruction (upadeśa) before roots beginning with consonants other than k and kh and not ending in ṣ.
Not [the n] of the roots bhā, bhū, pū, kam, gam, pyāy, and vep.
For any consonant except h (yar), a nasal sound (anunāsika) is optionally (vā) substituted before a nasal sound (anunāsika).
According to Śākaṭāyana, [no doubling occurs] in combinations of three or more consonants.
A sound homogeneous with the following replaces an anusvāra when followed by a yay sound.
After ud, [a sound homogeneous] with the preceding replaces the initial sound of sthā and stambh.
A circumflex accent replaces a low-pitched accent immediately following a high-pitched accent.
